newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU has grounds to appeal on WTO panel - Fischler.
newsitem.headline: EU has grounds to appeal on WTO panel - Fischler.

text.p: The European Union has good grounds for appealing against a World Trade Organisation ruling that the EU's banana import regime violated free trade rules, Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Wednesday.
"On the basis of our analysis of the (WTO dispute) panel and its report, we think we have good reasons to be able to oppose (the ruling)," Fischler told the European Parliament.

But he warned the EU would have to have a strong case if it made an appeal because if the process reconfirmed the WTO's original decision this would set an unfortunate legal precedent for future panels.

The commissioner said the EU had not finished studying the lengthy report setting out the reasons why the WTO believed the EU's preferential terms of trade with African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) banana producers conflicted with free trade rules.
The report could have serious implications for other aspects of EU trade, he warned.

German Christian Democrat Peter Kittlemann said he feared that if the countries challenging the EU banana regime -- the United States and four Latin American allies -- won their case, this would make it much easier for the U.S. to win WTO support to overturn the EU ban on imports of meat from animals treated with growth hormones.

Kittlemann urged the Commission and the Council of Ministers to seek a bilateral settlement with the U.S., similar to the deal which halted a US-EU clash in the WTO over a US law penalising foreign firms investing in Cuba.
